identity.title: Chest pain fully reproduced by palpation of chest wall

technique.how: Ask the patient to localise the pain, then press firmly over the sternum, costochondral junctions, ribs and parasternal muscles; ask whether the pressure reproduces the presenting pain exactly (not merely causes soreness). Inspect the tender area for a dermatomal vesicular rash (zoster) before attributing pain to the chest wall.
technique.prerequisites: Patient able to compare elicited pain with the presenting pain; ECG obtained regardless.
technique.contraindications: Recent chest trauma, sternotomy, or suspected rib fracture - palpate gently.

interpretation.positive_finding: Pain fully reproduced by chest-wall palpation lowers the probability of MI/ACS about four-fold (LR ~0.2-0.3; pooled 0.23), supporting a musculoskeletal cause, but only 5-10% of infarcts have this feature and it does not exclude ACS.
interpretation.negative_finding: Absence of reproducible tenderness is the norm in MI (present in ~92-94% of AMI/ACS) but is non-specific and barely raises the probability of ACS (LR+ ~1.5 or less).
interpretation.pitfalls: Partial or vague tenderness is common in ACS and PE, so insist on exact reproduction; PE and pericarditis can coexist with wall tenderness; a low-prevalence (primary care) setting is where the finding is most useful, whereas in a high-risk ED patient it should not stop the workup.
interpretation.changes_what: Positive: shift toward musculoskeletal/zoster causes, but still obtain ECG (and troponin if any ACS risk). Negative: no meaningful change in ACS probability.

estimates.population: Non-selected patients with chest pain (16 of 28 studies; primary care and ED populations pooled)
estimates.computed_from: Source reports the finding inverted ('absence of chest-wall tenderness': pooled sensitivity 92% [86-96], LR- 0.23 [0.18-0.29]). For tenderness PRESENT: sensitivity = 1-0.92 = 0.08 (CI 1-0.96, 1-0.86); LR+ for AMI = LR- of absence = 0.23 (0.18-0.29). Specificity of presence not reported in abstract.
estimates.quote: Absence of chest-wall tenderness on palpation had a LR- of 0.23 (95% CI = 0.18 to 0.29).
estimates.location: Abstract, Results (PubMed abstract; full text not accessible)

estimates.population: 893 consecutive patients with acute, undifferentiated chest pain at a UK ED chest pain unit (AMI 3.8%)
estimates.reference_standard: WHO criteria for AMI with 6-month follow-up
estimates.quote: pain radiating to the shoulder or both arms (LR = 4.07), and chest wall tenderness (LR = 0.3)

estimates.population: Patients with acute chest pain in studies pooled by the 1998 RCE
estimates.reference_standard: Clinical diagnosis of MI (ECG/enzymes per included studies)
estimates.computed_from: Not computed. RCE reports a between-study RANGE 0.2-0.4 with no pooled point estimate; value shown is the low end of the range, not a mean.
estimates.quote: chest pain reproduced by palpation (LR range, 0.2-0.4)
estimates.location: Abstract, Results (PubMed abstract; full text not accessible)

sources.citation: Bruyninckx R, Aertgeerts B, Bruyninckx P, Buntinx F. Signs and symptoms in diagnosing acute myocardial infarction and acute coronary syndrome: a diagnostic meta-analysis. Br J Gen Pract. 2008;58(547):105-111.
Goodacre S, Locker T, Morris F, Campbell S. How useful are clinical features in the diagnosis of acute, undifferentiated chest pain? Acad Emerg Med. 2002;9(3):203-208.
Panju AA, Hemmelgarn BR, Guyatt GH, Simel DL. The rational clinical examination. Is this patient having a myocardial infarction? JAMA. 1998;280(14):1256-1263.
Swap CJ, Nagurney JT. Value and limitations of chest pain history in the evaluation of patients with suspected acute coronary syndromes. JAMA. 2005;294(20):2623-2629.
Bösner S, Becker A, Abu Hani M, et al. Accuracy of symptoms and signs for coronary heart disease assessed in primary care. Br J Gen Pract. 2010;60(575):e246-e257.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use reproducible tenderness to forgo ECG/troponin in patients with high pretest probability (known CAD, ECG changes, diaphoresis, arm radiation); do not use after trauma or in suspected PE, where wall tenderness is common and uninformative.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: If the ECG is ischaemic or troponin is elevated, ignore the tenderness; a dermatomal rash or unilateral burning pain preceding a rash should prompt early antiviral treatment for zoster.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Reliability of chest-wall palpation not reported in the cited sources; the definition (fully vs partly reproduced) varies between studies and drives heterogeneity.

extraction_notes: The pooled figure comes from Bruyninckx 2008, whose abstract reports the sign inverted (absence of tenderness as a test for AMI); I converted to the 'tenderness present' direction (LR+ = 0.23; sensitivity = 0.08) and flagged computed=true with the arithmetic shown - no specificity is derivable from the abstract. ACS-target pooled sensitivity of absence (94%, 91-96) is in the same abstract but LR- for ACS is not separately quoted, so only the AMI entry was made. Panju 1998 gives a range (0.2-0.4) entered as low-end value with explicit note; Swap 2005 gives a combined range 0.2-0.3 across several 'atypical' features and is cited without a numeric entry. Bosner 2010 (primary care, n=1249) reports OR 0.27 (0.13-0.56) for CHD, not an LR, so cited only. No accuracy data located for tenderness as a discriminator of PE or zoster specifically.
